beats.what: The low-pressure system is expected to strengthen into a cyclonic storm by Oct 26 and cross the Andhra coast between Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam by the afternoon of Oct 28.
beats.why: Post-monsoon, the Bay of Bengal is warm and winds are favourable, so storms grow fast. East Telangana sits right in the rain path; Hyderabad is further west.
beats.care: Going to Khammam, Kothagudem, Bhadrachalam or Vizag on Oct 27–28? Push the trip if you can. In Hyderabad: no alert yet, dry till Oct 27.

cards.body: IMD has issued a red alert (heavy to very heavy rain) for Khammam, Bhadradri Kothagudem and Mulugu on Oct 28. Odisha has red alerts for Puri, Ganjam and Gajapati on Oct 27, with NDRF and ODRAF teams on standby.

cards.title: why the name 'Arnab' isn't official yet
cards.body: A storm gets the next name on the list only once it becomes a cyclonic storm. A September system that reached Andhra was a deep depression, so the name Arnab is still unused.
Hyderabad is likely to stay dry until Oct 27. The heaviest rain falls on the east side of Telangana, closest to the coast.

learn.t: Cyclone names come from a list made by 13 countries around the Indian Ocean and are used in order. A storm is named only when its winds reach cyclonic strength (63 km/h or more).
